title: Bringing a Companion to Türkiye for Medical Travel: Practical Guide
seoTitle: Medical Travel Companion in Türkiye: Practical Guide
metaDescription: Practical guide to bringing a medical travel companion to Türkiye: hospital guest beds, hotel rooms, airport transfers, and independent local support.
quickAnswer: Bringing a medical travel companion to Türkiye is optional for routine dental or hair procedures, yet strongly recommended after general anaesthesia or major surgery. Private Turkish hospitals typically provide a fold-out bed in single inpatient rooms, while hotels, transfers, and an independent local contact keep logistics manageable for both travellers.
category: Medical Travel to Türkiye — Independent Advisory & Safety (The ITO Standard)

body.text: Do you need a companion for dental, hair or surgical procedures?

Patients undergoing local-anaesthesia dental veneers, crowns, or hair transplants often travel solo without practical difficulty, provided hotel transfers are pre-booked. In contrast, anyone having general anaesthesia, rhinoplasty, body contouring, orthopaedic, or bariatric surgery benefits from a trusted companion for the first 48 to 72 hours after hospital discharge.

Your operating surgeon determines whether an escort is clinically required before discharge, as [U.S. Embassy guidance on medical tourism in Türkiye](https://tr.usembassy.gov/medical-tourism/) advises planning post-procedure support in advance. We coordinate your visit. Your licensed medical team makes clinical decisions. Even when a hospital allows solo discharge, a companion handles luggage, pharmacy errands, meal deliveries, and medication reminders while you rest.

body.text: What can a companion do during operation hours in Istanbul?

Most surgical procedures in Istanbul keep a patient in the operating theatre and recovery bay for four to eight hours. Companions rarely need to sit in a hospital lobby the entire time; most private hospitals register the companion's phone number and send a message when the patient returns to the inpatient room.

Before you fly, check the companion's passport validity and entry rules through the [Republic of Türkiye Ministry of Foreign Affairs visa portal](https://www.mfa.gov.tr/visa-information-for-foreigners.en.mfa) or [UK FCDO entry requirements for Türkiye](https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/turkey/entry-requirements). During operation hours, choose low-stress activities within 15 to 20 minutes of the hospital so traffic never delays your return:

items: Confirm the hospital update protocol: Ask the international patient desk who calls or messages when surgery finishes.
Stay in the same district: If the hospital is in Şişli, Nişantaşı, Ataşehir, or Bakırköy, walk to a nearby café, quiet park, or mall rather than crossing the Bosphorus.
Keep a local SIM or eSIM active: Reliable mobile data lets you receive clinic updates and order taxis quickly.
Prepare the recovery room: Pick up bottled water, electrolyte drinks, loose front-button clothing, and extra pillows before discharge.
Store emergency numbers: Save the hospital's 24-hour ward desk and Türkiye's 112 emergency line, noted in [GOV.UK health advice for Türkiye](https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/turkey/health).

body.text: How do hotel rooms, hospital guest beds and airport transfers work for two?

Private Turkish hospitals usually include one companion sofa-bed and basic meals inside a standard single inpatient room at no extra charge, though policies vary by hospital group. For hotels, book a twin-bed room or a junior suite rather than a standard double bed so the recovering patient sleeps undisturbed.

Airport logistics also change when two people travel with extra medical supplies and checked suitcases. At Istanbul Airport, non-travelling visitors or companions needing mobility help can check [iGA Istanbul Airport arrival passenger services](https://www.istairport.com/en/flights/airport-guides/arrival-passenger-guide/services/passenger-services/age-friendly-airport?locale=en), while faster terminal escort is available via [iGA Meet & Greet](https://www.igapass.com/en/iga-meet-and-greet-p-7000?locale=en). Always book a private Mercedes Vito or similar minivan rather than a standard saloon taxi so two passengers, two large bags, and a reclined seat fit comfortably. For return-day terminal tips, read our guide on [flying home after surgery in Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/flying-after-surgery-turkey).

faq.q: Can a companion stay overnight in a Turkish hospital room?
faq.a: Yes. Most private hospitals in Istanbul, Antalya, and İzmir include a fold-out bed for one companion inside a private inpatient room. Always confirm meal inclusion and visiting hours in writing before admission.

faq.q: Does a medical travel companion need a special visa for Türkiye?
faq.a: No special medical companion visa is needed for nationalities eligible for visa-free entry or standard e-Visa tourism stays. Check passport rules on the official Ministry of Foreign Affairs website before booking flights.

faq.q: Should we book one double bed or two twin beds at the hotel?
faq.a: Book twin beds or a suite with a separate sofa bed. Post-surgical patients often sleep propped upright with extra pillows and wake frequently for medication, so separate beds protect both travellers' rest.

faq.q: Do clinic packages charge extra for a companion's hotel stay?
faq.a: Many clinics include one companion in the same hotel room at little or no extra room cost, though breakfast, airport transfer upgrades, and flights remain separate. Confirm companion surcharges in writing before paying.

faq.q: What if I have to travel solo for surgery in Türkiye?
faq.a: If no companion can travel, tell your surgeon before booking so they can confirm whether solo discharge is safe. Consider extending your inpatient hospital stay by an extra night or hiring a licensed private recovery nurse.
